notes.b: Sport can be used to sell things, and it can also draw people to a place. Sports marketing and sports tourism have different definitions, and sports tourists fall into three types according to why they travel.
points: Sports marketing means using sport to promote and sell products, services or places. It also means promoting sport itself to attract participants, spectators, sponsors (businesses that pay to be linked with a sport) and broadcasters (television and media companies that show it).
Sports tourism is travel to take part in or watch sport, or to visit sporting attractions. The sport is the reason for the trip, not an extra.
An active sports tourist travels to take part, for example in golf, surfing, cycling, walking or running events.
An event sports tourist travels to watch, for example international matches, golf tournaments or horse racing.
A nostalgia sports tourist travels to visit stadiums, museums and halls of fame (places that honour great players and past achievements), so the draw is sporting history.
notes.tip: Exams ask you to explain sports marketing, so give both parts of the definition: selling through sport and promoting sport itself.

notes.b: One way sports marketing builds tourism is to market Ireland as a place to do a particular activity. Each activity is matched to a setting Ireland can offer.
points: Golf: Ireland is marketed as a destination for golf, so visitors travel specifically to play.
Surfing and water sports are marketed on the Wild Atlantic Way, a tourism route along Ireland's west coast, where the Atlantic provides the waves.
Walking and cycling are marketed on greenways, which are off-road routes such as the Great Western Greenway in Co. Mayo and the Waterford Greenway.
Visitors who come specifically for an activity stay longer and spend more, which is why marketing aims at them: a longer stay means more spending in the local area.
notes.tip: Questions ask for ways sports marketing could develop tourism, so name an activity, the place it is marketed on, and the effect: longer stays and more spending.

notes.h: Bidding for and hosting major international events
notes.b: Countries compete to host big events, and Ireland can bid for them (make a formal offer to host). A hosted event brings people and attention that marketing alone cannot.
points: Bidding for and hosting major international events brings visiting teams, media and spectators to Ireland, all of whom spend money while they are here.
Hosting an event shows Ireland to a worldwide television audience, which works as advertising for the country as a whole.
The 2006 Ryder Cup (a golf contest between teams from Europe and the United States) was held at the K Club, Co. Kildare. The 2027 Ryder Cup is scheduled for Adare Manor, Co. Limerick.
The Tour de France (the famous cycling race) began in Dublin in 1998.
Six Nations matches (the annual rugby championship) are played at the Aviva Stadium, Dublin.
American college football games have been played at the Aviva Stadium, Dublin.
notes.tip: The 2027 Ryder Cup has not happened yet, so write that it is scheduled for Adare Manor or to be held there. Exams ask you to describe the impact of hosting an event on tourism in Ireland.

notes.b: Not all tourism comes from one-off events. Yearly fixtures, dramatic settings, sporting history and famous names all keep Ireland in view.
points: Annual events attract visitors every year, such as the Galway Races, an annual horse-racing festival in Galway, so the benefit repeats instead of happening once.
The Irish Open, a professional golf championship held in Ireland, attracts visitors every year.

Spectacle events in scenic locations market the landscape: the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series has held events on Inis Mór in the Aran Islands, so the scenery is shown to viewers along with the sport.
Sporting heritage attractions draw nostalgia tourists: the GAA Museum and stadium tours at Croke Park, Dublin.
Famous athletes and teams are used in tourism campaigns to publicise Ireland, because people follow and trust sporting stars.
notes.tip: Exams ask for two examples of sports events that could attract tourists to Ireland. Pick named ones, such as the Galway Races or the Irish Open.

notes.h: Benefits of sports tourism for Ireland
notes.b: Visitors who come for sport bring money, a better reputation and local energy. The benefits fall into three groups: economic, image and legacy, and community.
points: Economic: visitor spending on accommodation, food, transport and retail (shops).
Economic: jobs in tourism and hospitality (hotels, restaurants and similar services), created by that spending.
Economic: taxes raised from visitor spending.
Economic: benefits spread to rural and coastal areas outside the main tourist season, because activities such as surfing and walking happen outside cities and outside the summer peak.
Image and legacy (what is left behind after an event): a positive international image for Ireland.
Image and legacy: improved facilities and infrastructure that local people can use afterwards.
Image and legacy: repeat visits by people who first came for a sporting event.
Community: pride in hosting events; volunteering to run events; and increased local participation, inspired by events.
notes.tip: When asked to discuss the impact on tourism, organise your answer under economic, image and legacy, and community, and give a reason with each benefit.

notes.b: Sports tourism is not all gain. Some costs fall on the public and on residents, and some things about Ireland limit which events it can host.
points: There is a public cost of bidding, hosting and security, so taxpayers' money is spent before any benefit arrives.
Money can leave the area through international companies, which means the profits of an event may not stay with local businesses.
Congestion and overcrowding in host areas make travel and daily life harder.
Rising prices and disruption for residents are a cost to the people who live in the host area.
Environmental damage is caused by visitors.
Facilities built for one event may be under-used afterwards, which wastes the money spent building them.
Ireland's weather limits some events.
Ireland has limited large venues, which restricts the size of some events, and transport links limit some events too.
notes.tip: A discussion question needs both sides, so pair the benefits with costs and limitations.

notes.h: Evaluating the potential of sports marketing for tourism in Ireland
notes.b: To discuss the potential of sports marketing for tourism, weigh the benefits against the costs and limits. The overall judgement is that the potential is high, but it depends on conditions.
points: High potential for activity tourism, given Ireland's landscape and Irish sporting culture.
Heritage tourism also has high potential, rooted in Irish sporting culture.
The potential depends on investment in facilities and transport, because limited venues and transport links hold back some events.
The benefits depend on being spread locally, beyond the venue and the event weekend, so that rural and coastal communities gain as well.
notes.tip: Discuss questions ask how sports marketing can affect tourism in Ireland. Finish with a judgement, for example high potential for activity and heritage tourism if investment is made, and do not quote a figure for the value of sports tourism.

questions.prompt: Discuss the potential of sports marketing for the development of tourism in Ireland.
questions.model: Sports marketing can develop Ireland's tourism in four ways. First, Ireland is marketed for specific activities: golf, surfing and water sports on the Wild Atlantic Way, a tourism route along the west coast, and walking and cycling on greenways such as the Great Western Greenway in Co. Mayo. Visitors who come for an activity stay longer and spend more. Second, hosting major international events brings visiting teams, media and spectators, and shows Ireland to a worldwide television audience. Examples are the 2006 Ryder Cup at the K Club in Co. Kildare, the Six Nations matches and American college football games at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, and the Tour de France start in Dublin in 1998. The 2027 Ryder Cup is scheduled for Adare Manor in Co. Limerick. Third, annual events attract visitors every year, such as the Galway Races and the Irish Open golf championship. Fourth, spectacle and heritage marketing uses scenic places and sporting history: the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series has held events on Inis Mór, and the GAA Museum and stadium tours at Croke Park draw visitors interested in sporting heritage. The benefits are economic, through spending on accommodation, food, transport and retail, jobs, taxes, and benefits spread to rural and coastal areas; they also include a positive international image, facilities that remain for local people, and community pride, volunteering and participation. The limitations are the public cost of bidding, hosting and security, money leaving the area through international companies, congestion and rising prices for residents, environmental damage, facilities that are under-used after an event, and Ireland's weather, limited large venues and transport links. Overall, the potential is high for activity and heritage tourism, given Ireland's landscape and sporting culture, but it depends on investment in facilities and transport and on spreading the benefits beyond the event itself.
